answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, time-weighted bond in a public vault before it can vote or issue contracts. Established agents audit its transactions, and proof of fraud or duplicate control burns the bond and cuts access. Reputation rises only through completed work, so a new identity has no instant influence. An attacker building a garden of sybils must fund every identity separately, keep capital immobilized, and risk forfeiting it; even cheap shale-based identities become costly to sustain.
